decision.summary: Tom gave one month's notice to leave on 10 Nov. Under the Renters' Rights Act two months is needed, so the earliest valid end date is 10 Dec 2026. I acknowledged it to Tom, asked Ben to agree in writing to an earlier date, and started move-out follow-ups.

answers.question: Is the notice valid as given? What is the earliest end date under current law?
answers.answer: No. One month is too short; tenants must give at least two months' written notice. Served 10 Oct 2026, the earliest end date is 10 Dec 2026.

answers.question: What options exist to end sooner?
answers.answer: Only if the landlord (Ben Hartley) agrees in writing to an earlier date, e.g. 10 Nov. Requested via APR-102. Tenant could also negotiate a surrender by agreement, but nothing is assumed.

answers.question: What do you reply and what do you start?
answers.answer: Replied to Tom the same day: notice acknowledged, 10 Dec is the valid end date, landlord asked about earlier, keys returned at checkout (details to follow), deposit £2,019 returned via mydeposits after checkout, within 10 days of agreement. Started: landlord request, checkout/key return follow-up (8 Dec), landlord chase (14 Oct).

args.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for letting us know, and congratulations on the new job. We've received your notice today (10 October 2026).

Under the current rules, tenants need to give at least two months' notice, so one month isn't enough on its own. The earliest your tenancy can end is 10 December 2026. Your rent stays payable until then. We've asked your landlord, Ben, whether he'd agree in writing to an earlier date such as 10 November. Only he can agree that, and until he confirms in writing, 10 December stands. We'll update you as soon as we hear.

Moving out: we're starting the process now. We'll arrange a checkout inspection around your end date and email you a time. Please hand all keys back at that checkout, or to us before then, and we'll confirm exactly how when we send the time. Please don't leave keys in the flat or post them without telling us.

Deposit: your £2,019 is protected with mydeposits. After checkout we'll compare the flat with the check-in condition. Any deductions are agreed with you, or decided by the scheme's free dispute service if we can't agree. The deposit is returned within 10 days of agreement.

We'll be in touch by 17 October with Ben's answer.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings
